news.title: Bombay HC clears construction on two Pune Cantonment leasehold plots
news.para: The Bombay High Court has permitted residential building on leasehold plots in Pune Cantonment, mandating that defence authorities grant construction permits within a month. The ruling emphasizes that future defence requirements cannot compromise the rights of current leaseholders. These leases remain in effect until 2033, but renewals are uncertain. Meanwhile, defence authorities are considering legal avenues to contest this decision.

news.title: Redevelopment gains can’t be taxed in hands of CHS, rules Mumbai ITAT
news.para: The Mumbai ITAT has annulled a contentious Rs 18.4 crore tax addition for a housing society, stating the society served merely as a representative for its flat owners. The tribunal observed that the transactions reported under the society's PAN weren't its own revenues, given that no sale proceeds appeared in its bank account. This decision will benefit housing societies engaged in redevelopment projects.

news.title: Buildings ‘unsafe’ for years, Noida authority now pastes vacate notices after Satya Niketan collapse
news.para: The Noida Authority is issuing vacate notices for 56 unsafe buildings that have been flagged as dilapidated for years. With these structures situated in crowded neighborhoods, residents are left in a state of uncertainty. Following a severe collapse in 2018, the authority had initially conducted a survey, highlighting numerous unauthorized buildings. Previous demolition efforts were largely ineffective, leading to current notices being sent for many of the same properties.

news.title: EWS certificates, land division go online in Uttar Pradesh; khatauni records made simpler
news.para: Uttar Pradesh's revenue services have taken a significant leap forward with the launch of three innovative digital portals. These platforms streamline the application processes for EWS certificates and land divisions, enabling applicants to easily monitor their submissions online from initiation to completion. A revamped khatauni will facilitate clearer understanding of land records for common owners, thus enhancing transparency and reducing bureaucratic hassle in these essential services.

news.title: State-wide drive to fix land record errors from September 15: Bihar minister
news.para: Bihar will launch a 45-day campaign starting September 15 to fix land records.  This initiative aims to correct errors in khata, khesra numbers, and plot details.  Officials are directed to proactively assist citizens with their land record applications.  The department will also establish land banks and introduce special mutation procedures.  New survey districts will provide maps with land records to minimize future disputes.

news.title: HC pulls up government & Ghaziabad development body for  handing over Gulmohar Greens flats without CC
news.para: The Allahabad High Court has criticized state authorities and the Ghaziabad Development Authority.  They allowed flat possession without mandatory completion certificates, which is a legal violation.  The court rejected an incomplete affidavit and demanded a better one by September 14.  Authorities must also ensure compliance with construction and completion certificate laws.  This case stems from a residents' petition filed against the developer in 2025.

news.title: Gujarat assembly passes  rent bill 2026 to balance landlord and tenant rights
news.para: Gujarat's Assembly passed three significant bills during its Monsoon session. The Rent Bill 2026 aims to balance landlord and tenant rights with mandatory agreements. Ease of Doing Business Bill 2026 reduces regulatory burdens and promotes self-declaration. The Land Holdings Bill 2026 regularizes past violations and sets minimum land areas. These reforms intend to improve ease of living and doing business across the state.

news.title: SC sets four-year deadline to raze, rebuild Chintels Pradiso's complex
news.para: The Supreme Court has mandated that Chintels Paradiso be entirely demolished and rebuilt, with the redevelopment of the Sector 109 housing complex set to start in March 2027. Residents are required to vacate unsafe towers by January 2027 to finalize contractual agreements. Sobha is slated to manage the redevelopment, which will introduce six new towers, with homeowners contributing Rs 1,000 per square foot for their new units.

news.title: Ghaziabad: GDA seeks public objections on Indirapuram extension, notifies 150 acres for acquisition
news.para: The Ghaziabad Development Authority has announced a public objection period for its long-awaited Indirapuram Extension Scheme. This ambitious project, which spans 153 acres, has faced hurdles in the form of farmer litigation concerning land compensation for the last twenty years. Recent revisions to building bylaws support vertical expansion with taller buildings, promising substantial revenue generation for the authority.

news.title: Haryana RERA orders Vatika to pay ₹22.7 lakh to homebuyers over flat delay
news.para: Haryana Rera has ruled that Vatika Ltd must pay over Rs 22 lakh to homebuyers for an alarming six-year delay in delivering their promised residential units. Additionally, the authority has granted Rs 1 lakh for the emotional suffering endured by the buyers. Despite multiple reassurances and deadline extensions from the developer, they did not fulfill their commitments, leading to this ruling that also stipulates interest on the compensation sum.

news.title: UK's homebuilder Berkeley urges property tax cuts as buyers stay cautious
news.para: British homebuilder Berkeley Group urges government to cut property taxes. Cautious buyers keep housing demand subdued as the budget approaches. Rivals also called for lower stamp duty and government support. Prime Minister Andy Burnham denied plans to reduce stamp duty. Builders curb land buying and slow construction due to market strains.

news.title: ED raids against Gaya-based Ramnandi Hotels and Resorts & promoters in bank 'fraud' case
news.para: The Enforcement Directorate has carried out searches in numerous locations across India as part of a money laundering investigation targeting a hotel group from Gaya. This probe is linked to a suspected bank loan fraud involving Rs 131.79 crore. Officials believe the group may have manipulated financial documents to divert funds and are also examining the questionable sale of mortgaged properties at below-market prices.

news.title: Kotak Realty Fund to invest ₹800 crore in Smartworld Developers' two projects in Gurugram
news.para: Kotak Realty Fund will invest about ₹800 crore in Phase I of its partnership with Smartworld Developers. The investment will support Smartworld Sky Arc and Trump Residences in Sector 69, Gurugram, which together have a GDV of over ₹8,200 crore.

news.title: Construction of houses for Wayanad rehabilitation to be completed by Oct-end: Minister
news.para: The construction of homes in the Wayanad rehabilitation township is on track, with a completion date set for the end of October. The contractor is focused on delivering all 110 houses as planned. Additionally, a review will allow for the inclusion of disaster victims initially overlooked. By December, basic infrastructure work will be completed, followed by a beneficiary selection process via a draw.

news.title: Patna civic body launches 15-day drive to recover ₹80 crore property tax due
news.para: The Patna Municipal Corporation has launched a dedicated fifteen-day campaign to assess property taxes. This initiative focuses on incorporating unassessed properties while also re-evaluating existing ones. The goal is to recover around eighty crore rupees in outstanding tax payments. Special teams will prioritize new assessments and target major defaulters, utilizing electricity consumer data to discover properties that have evaded taxation.

news.title: Delhi: Only three PG buildings out of 1,355 found 'visibly dangerous' in MCD survey, nine found repairable
news.para: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has conducted a survey revealing three hazardous paying-guest buildings, housing a total of sixty-nine residents who urgently need relocation. Additionally, nine more structures were marked for substantial repairs. Reflecting heightened vigilance post the recent collapse in Satya Niketan, authorities have demolished 111 properties and sealed off 88 within just four days.

news.title: Nagpur civic body rules out amnesty to defaulters as tax recovery drive gathers pace
news.para: The Nagpur Municipal Corporation has turned down a proposed property tax amnesty scheme. This decision coincides with their intensified campaign to recover outstanding dues from major defaulters. The standing committee chairperson highlighted the importance of fairness to diligent taxpayers. As part of their strategy, the civic body is now proceeding with property seizures and issuing warnings about possible service disconnections.

news.title: DDA holds consultations on Delhi master plan 2047 implementation
news.para: The Delhi Development Authority has initiated discussions regarding the implementation of the Master Plan for Delhi 2047. Key focus areas included enhancing inter-departmental collaboration and strategies for transport-oriented development. Additionally, notable conversations covered topics such as industrial zones, infrastructure growth, heritage conservation, and land pooling, all aimed at ensuring a synchronized approach towards effective execution of the Master Plan.

news.title: In Noida’s PG belt, buildings rise nine floors where two are allowed, cables dangle at arms reach
news.para: Noida villages are experiencing a worrying rise in illegal multi-storey paying guest accommodations, which frequently disregard necessary fire safety measures and emergency exits. Many of these properties flout building codes, raising valid structural safety concerns. Despite this, tenants, mainly students and IT workers, often compromise their safety for lower rents and convenience, perpetuating a cycle of unchecked construction driven by high demand.

news.title: Delhi high court fixes deadline for final property conversion policy
news.para: The Delhi High Court has rebuked government authorities for their sluggishness regarding the leasehold to freehold property conversion policy. With a looming deadline for submissions set for the September twenty-eighth hearing, countless residents continue to endure unacceptable delays. The court pointed out the disarray in inter-departmental communication and the stalled applications, even as conversion fees have been collected by the DDA.
